topic.title: Why Time Feels Faster Every Year

copy.title: WHY YOUR YEARS KEEP SHRINKING

steps.rule: Notice when the week blurred past
steps.why: you cannot fix a leak you have not located yet.

steps.rule: Count how many firsts you had
steps.why: the brain compresses repeated days into a single memory file.

steps.rule: Name one thing that felt genuinely new
steps.why: a single novel moment anchors the whole week as distinct.

steps.rule: Schedule one unfamiliar thing per week
steps.why: new encoding stretches perceived time the way sleep stretches a night.

steps.rule: Review the month against your list
steps.why: density of distinct memories is the only way to slow the clock down.

copy.kicker: Same days, same blur, smaller life.
copy.thumb_scene: Wick stands on a plain white studio background facing the camera, holding a plain wall calendar with most days crossed out in identical red marks, one single day left uncrossed, his finger resting on that one open square, expression sharp and deliberate.
copy.send_to: the friend who just said the year went nowhere again
